videos.script: At the end of lesson 4 the collection could send every request. It could not tell you whether a single answer was right. {{collection}} You still had to read each one, and paste a token by hand. This lesson gives every request a few lines of JavaScript that run after the answer arrives. {{script}} Each one is a named check. The status is 201. The location header is there. The order says confirmed. {{checks}} Then the requests start passing things along. The token request saves the token, and the order requests use it. {{chain}} The new order's address is saved too, so the next request reads the right order. A script can also run before a request, to make a fresh key or a fresh token. {{before}} One request can run many times, once per line of a file of seat counts. {{data}} And some checks are worse than none. They pass once and fail every time after. {{brittle}} One test fails on purpose. It is the defect you found in lesson 1, and now it has a name. {{head}}
